work_units.notes:
textcharts added `subject: str | None = None` to all chart constructors.
When set, the title is composed as f"{subject} {default_title}".

Example: `subject="Query Latency"` on Histogram → "Query Latency Histogram"

Current BenchBox pattern:
  `ASCIIQueryHistogram(data=data, title="Query Latency Histogram", ...)`
Could become:
  `ASCIIQueryHistogram(data=data, subject="Query Latency", ...)`

Evaluate for each of the ~14 constructor calls in ascii_runtime.py whether
subject= would be cleaner. The benefit is avoiding title string duplication
with the chart type name. The risk is titles that don't compose well with
the generic default (e.g., subject="Performance" + "Bar Chart" = "Performance
Bar Chart" - fine, but subject="Phase Breakdown by Platform" + "Stacked
Breakdown" = nonsense).

Decision criteria:
- Use subject= when the domain qualifier composes naturally with the generic
  chart type name (e.g., "Query Latency" + "Histogram" → good)
- Keep explicit title= when the desired title doesn't match the pattern
  (e.g., "Cost vs Performance" doesn't compose with "Scatter Plot")
- Keep explicit title= for dynamic titles (f-strings with platform names)

Done criteria: Adopt subject= if 5+ of the ~14 call sites compose cleanly.
If fewer than 5 compose well, skip - the consistency benefit is too small
to justify a mixed approach (some subject=, some title=). Document the
evaluation result either way in a commit message or code comment.

Scope: ascii_runtime.py constructor calls only. Do NOT touch MCP dispatch
or exporters.py - those pass title= from external input and must remain
explicit.
work_units.summary: Evaluate adopting subject= parameter for cleaner title composition
